src: I commend the curiosity, even though the matter at hand seems elusive when trying to capture its essence in words.
What I name the Urge covers the underlying motivation of living beings on this planet, the intensity of what drives them. The quality of their longing.
Like an instinct?

Sort of. The topic might sound philosophical or psychological, but what's fascinating, and why I began with this research in the first place, is the biological aspect to it, its pertinence to this planet.
It is no mere intellectual thing. It's something in the air, or in the flesh. It might even be related to the humanoid mutations.
Artus seems to be concerned about you.
He's sweet. He's the best that ever happened to me and I know that I am giving him a hard time for it.
I neglect him, spend less time with him, and he is, of course, concerned. I would be, too.
But work is important. This work here especially. Not only for my own understanding of the mess Nexus is in, but also, potentially, for the greater benefit of our community.
I wish Artus had a better understanding of the importance of this research. But he's a bit too short-sighted for that.
Ah, sorry, I shouldn't talk like that. He understands much more than I give him credit for.
So what happens now?
What happens now is that I will expose myself to the pheromones of the worm and measure the result.
Maybe we should do this later.
Alright. But let's not wait too long.
I think Artus should do this.
I don't think that this is a good idea.
But I do.
I feel a bit dizzy. I think it's working.
Hmmh.
This was not what I intended. But I guess it will be sufficient data for the experiment now.
Go on then, perform your experiment.
Let's start.
Come here now.
Ouch.
That hurt.
But this will give me enough data to proceed with my research.
No, you won't.
Ira! You shouldn't do this. It's dangerous to your health. Let me inhale it instead.
But... No. Artus, you mean well, but it's my own experiment, and I should bear the brunt of it. Especially if it turns out to be harmful.
Let us proceed as planned.
Actually, I took care of the issue already.
What? But...
Let me examine you.
Astonishing. You speak the truth. I mean, your assessment is actually correct.
I thank you.
Here, take this as a token of my gratitude.
I thank you, too.
I have that rare specimen you were looking for.
Ah, perfect. Let's see what we can do with this.
Thank you.
I'll be ready in a minute.
You are supposed to get me a rare specimen from the park.
It's a worm with a brighter complexion than usual.
Alright. Got it.
I think your field unit is filled up now.
Excellent news. Let me take a look.
Yes. That will do.
Now, while I begin analyzing the data, you are free to progress with the next step of our experiment.
Your task will be to acquire a rare specimen.
It's a Fleshworm, more peaceful than the regular kind. I caught one in the park ages ago, but it didn't survive for long.
Hey, you could have told me about this worm when you sent me out with the field unit.
I guess I could have. But I was unsure about the multi-tasking capabilities of my new assistant.
Getting that worm is crucial now. I gathered some pheromone from the previous worm but the amount I have left will not be sufficient.
Ira. What are you doing?
Giving instructions to my assistant.
I won't let you get harmed again by one of these worms.
Please, Ira, this is too dangerous.
I... Look, we will be careful. I promise. Let's acquire the worm first, and then we'll decide on how best to proceed.
Best to search the park for this worm. It's a worm with a brighter complexion than the ones you might already be familiar with.
Uhm. Alright. I'll take a look.
Actually...
Place the field unit I gave you close to aggressive or otherwise aroused mutants.
Ah, yes. Sure.
Alright. How can I assist you?
What do you need?
I need someone with enough panache for actual field work in direct vicinity of the ill ones.
The ill ones?
The mutants. I need to gather data from them when they are under a spell of aggression or a similar kind of excitement.
I'll give you a field unit. Your task is to set up that unit and arouse the interest of nearby mutants.
You look resourceful enough to find your way to some appropriate specimens.
Uhm. I don't think so. Maybe later.
Well. OK.
OK. I'll do this.
Great. This pleases me immensly.
Here's the field unit. It's the only one I have, so take care and don't lose it.
How does it work?
Place it on the ground near the mutant targets and it should begin gathering data on its own. For this to work the targets need to exhibit aggressive behavior or act in a similar state of arousal.
Alright. Understood.
That's unfair, Ira.
It's honest. You always remind me to be honest.
But back to the matter at hand.
Let me prepare this.
I don't feel so good.
Artus...
[She sobs.]
I guard my boys 'ere.
Have to be careful of 'em shamans.
Meat.
Meeeaaaat!
Meat. Meat.
MEAT!
AGONY. I remember you.
How are you feeling?
PAIN. RESENTMENT. I am well and I am unwell.
Alone and forever. Biding my time here, outside.
Because she banished me.
Or did I go on my own?
Wanted to feel what she felt. Together as one.
Now I am feeling all of this on my own. The pain. The offerings of my flesh and blood. The ecstasy.
PAIN. I am feeling better now.
And this is because of you. GRATITUDE.
But I am still alone here.
I am looking for a flavor, a certain piece of meat.
PAIN. Flesh and blood, and no feelings left.
Once. Once have known the pleasure, the sensuation of bodies, joined, and tasting her flesh.
My own flesh. Tasting my own flesh. RESENTMENT.
You are asking me because you want a piece of my body.
I guess so.
Do you really need this?
Yes, I do.
Embrace that part of me then.
Ahh, sweet pain. Constant companion.
But this one you earned, so it's freely given, even more so than the other.
I want to visit Mother on behalf of a... friend.
MOTHER. My wife. She is still mad at me.
Or is she not?
Forgiveness. Go to her, and ask her.
I want to talk to Mother on behalf of the humans.
MOTHER!
{He gets agitated.}
Alone. Left alone. Left her alone, and now there's eternal regret.
HUMANS. Human once. I remember how it was.
I remember Mother, too. All the sentiments, stored away, in my cave of regret.
Can you help me with entering the temple?
HUMANS. Human once. They are a cause of great suffering.
No help at all during all these years.
Just devouring my innards, perpetually.
No good-will left.
PAIN. IMMORTAL PAIN. This is me suffering.
I cannot cope anymore. It is too much. PAIN.
This is horrible. Why are they cutting you up like that?
MEAT. I AM MEAT. They need me.
They need all of us. But me, here, in this city, especially.
I feed them. FEED THEM.
Shall I... shall I stop them?
STOP THEM. MAKE THEM SUFFER.
No, don't make them suffer.
But please, please make them stop.
MAKE THEM SUFFER.
How can I stop them?
AGONIZING. Make them stop.
I do not care about the how. KILL THEM.
Please don't kill them.
You're sending mixed signals here.
KILL THEM. I can't help it.
I am not myself anymore. KILL THEM.
Please don't kill them.
What is this place?
It's Mother's abode. Her temple.
In the past this has been a place of nurturing and caretaking. Of community.
But that time is long gone now since Mother ended her service to the community, and since Morrowmeat took over that role.
Can I see Mother?
No, an audience will not be granted.
Your entering is a sacrilege to this place and Mother's children will kill you if you disturb their rest.
Intruder!
Your presence is not welcome here.
An audience will not be granted.
Welcome back, my child.
Who are you?
I am Mother. I have lived here in this city since the Bleeding. My children built this temple for me.
I was their provider for a long time. That is, until Morrowmeat came along.
You have met him already. Otherwise I wouldn't have let you in.
How is he?
I don't know.
It's hard to make sense of him. He was hard to read even back when he was still walking around, ostensibly sane.
He's miserable.
Yes, I expected him to be.
I was angry at him for a long while. I still am. But I also realized that he was probably sick already before we even met the first time.
This fate of ours, he should not have longed for it.
He's fine.
Really? That surprises me.
I think you might be dishonest with me.
Why are you down here in this place?
I was tired. I still am.
A load of pain, then disappointment. A lack of direction. No meaning, no sense.
Also sorrow and abandonment. I wanted to take care of the children, but they didn't need me anymore.
So I severed myself from the outside world. Only Hevla was allowed down here, and the occasional guest, thanks to my curiosity.
Hevla?
Yes. Hevla. She's gone now. I fear she might be in trouble.
Do you know the Feeder? A wandering flesh-machine-thing?
I think I know whom you mean. I haven't seen him with my own eyes. But my servants told me about him.
What's your business with that Feeder? Why are you looking for him?
[Shrug.]
The silent type. This is fine. I won't make you tell.
As for myself, the Feeder looks like a troublemaker. More than that even. He spells doom.
The Feeder tried to enter the villa. Hevla's villa. I don't know if he succeeded or not.
This is what troubles me: Hevla left the city some time ago. And the Feeder seems to have left the city, too, now. I fear the worst.
He's killing other Titans.
Hmmh.
You care about us?
Yes, I can smell your type. You are not so different than us.
I got involved.
A commendable trait among humans, getting involved.
I like that. I wish that all my children were a bit more active.
About Hevla...
Yes?
So who's Hevla?
